samples.scenario: Compromised firmware update for a popular network switch vendor includes hidden functionality that accepts encrypted commands from attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling persistent remote access and network reconnaissance.

version_control_commit_log.author: devops@netswitchvendor.com
version_control_commit_log.message: Firmware update: security patch and performance improvements

samples.detection_method: Analyze firmware update packages for unauthorized code insertions via binary diffing and signature validation; monitor network traffic from updated devices for unusual encrypted outbound connections on uncommon ports; implement integrity checks on firmware versions and verify cryptographic signatures; deploy anomaly-based IDS to detect command and control traffic patterns from network devices.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

samples.scenario: A compromised third-party cloud SDK package used for authentication introduces logic that silently logs user credentials and sends them to an attacker-controlled API endpoint during token refresh operations.

version_control_commit_log.author: alice.jones <alice.jones@trustedvendor.com>
version_control_commit_log.message: Enhance token refresh to support new auth flows

samples.detection_method: Perform static code analysis on SDK packages before deployment; verify the integrity of third-party dependencies via SBOM and hash validation; monitor and alert on unusual outbound HTTPS POST requests from client applications to unknown external domains, especially during authentication flows; use endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to flag suspicious network activity originating from SDK runtime environments.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

samples.scenario: A trusted hardware component supplier's firmware update for network devices is compromised, embedding a hidden rootkit that activates on boot to create a covert channel for remote attackers to manipulate device configurations and intercept traffic.

version_control_commit_log.message: Firmware update version 3.5.0 with security patches

samples.detection_method: Validate firmware updates via cryptographic signatures and compare SBOM hashes; monitor unusual open ports and persistent TCP listeners on network devices; capture network traffic for uncommon destination IPs and ports; implement host-based intrusion detection on devices to detect unexpected process hooks; audit version control commits from third-party suppliers for suspicious code introducing persistent backdoors.

samples.scenario: A third-party development tool integrated into the CI/CD pipeline is compromised. The malicious update injects a script that collects developer credentials and environment secrets, sending them via encrypted DNS queries to an attacker-controlled domain.

network_iocs: DNS TXT queries with base64 encoded payload

samples.detection_method: Monitor DNS traffic for abnormal TXT queries containing base64 or encoded secrets; inspect version control commits for added network calls to suspicious domains; enforce environment variable encryption and restrict access in CI/CD environments; implement policies to detect unauthorized scripts in build tools; use endpoint detection to flag DNS queries with unusual patterns and unexpected external resolutions from build servers.
